newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tells Kabila aid is conditional on rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells Kabila aid is conditional on rights.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday warned self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila of the new Democratic Republic of Congo that world support for his rule would depend on his concern for democracy and human rights.

"We have hopes, but we are watching very carefully" the actions of Kabila, whose rebel forces ousted Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko at the weekend and renamed the country, Albright told a dockside news conference during a visit to the port of Wilmington, Delaware.
"We are making it very clear that it is important for the new government to be inclusive, to be concerned and do a lot about democratic practices and human rights," Albright said.
"We are going to continue to make that clear and make it also evident that large-scale support by the international community will depend on the way that those three criteria are met," she added.
Albright appeared to be referring to financial aid to the new government. Washington has already expressed displeasure at the way Kabila's forces have treated Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire.
The United States has repeatedly called for elections to be held in Zaire.

Earlier, the State Department in Washington said that U.S. ambassador in Kinshasa Daniel Simpson met Monday morning with two aides to Kabila, and they agreed to establish "ongoing contacts" between the U.S. embassy and the new leadership.
Kabila is expected to arrive in Kinshasa Tuesday. Mobutu has fled the country and is believed to be in Morocco, U.S. officials said.
